name: AMD Helios (72x MI455X)
generation: Instinct MI400 series (MI455X, CDNA 5) + EPYC Venice (Zen 6)
availability: Full production since July 2026; first shipments expected by end of Q3 2026, volume deployments 2H 2026. AMD reference design built by OEM/ODM partners (e.g. HPE, Supermicro, Celestica); figures can vary by OEM.
description: Double-wide OCP Open Rack Wide (ORW) rack, 44 OU, 18 liquid-cooled compute trays (4x MI455X + 1x EPYC Venice SP7 + up to 12x Pensando Vulcano 800G AI NICs + 1x Pensando Salina 400G DPU each) and 6 liquid-cooled scale-up switch trays (2x 512-lane 200G UALoE switch ASICs each, Broadcom Tomahawk 6 class; HPE builds use Juniper QFX5252) forming one 72-GPU UALink-over-Ethernet domain. Power: in-rack power shelves feed a 50 V DC liquid-cooled vertical busbar at the rear; no Helios-specific 800 V DC input has been published (ORW allows side power racks, but this is not confirmed for Helios), so only ac_54v is listed. Cooling: rear blind-mate quick-disconnect manifolds to the facility loop (~385 L/min reported). The 2.4 Tb/s-per-GPU scale-out figure assumes 3 NICs per GPU; a 2-NIC-per-GPU option exists (144 ports).

nominal_power_w.note: press report (The Register and StorageReview, 23 July 2026): rack draws 225-245 kW depending on workload. AMD has not published a rack power figure. An early Introl blog figure of ~140 kW predates launch and is disregarded.

peak_power_w.note: AMD/Schneider Electric Helios reference design (Reference Design 121) supports racks up to 246 kW; used as the planning peak. No EDPp or transient figure published; sub-second GPU transients may exceed this.

power_shelves.note: AMD describes in-rack power shelves feeding a vertical 50 V DC busbar but publishes no shelf count as of 2026-10.

shelf_rating_w.note: power shelf rating not published by AMD or OEMs as of 2026-10.

liquid_fraction.note: AMD/Schneider reference design says its CDU-based and hybrid air/liquid cooling removes up to 84% of heat (lower bound). AMD and press describe compute trays, switch trays and the busbar as liquid-cooled, so the real share may be higher; upper bound is an assumption.

max_coolant_supply_c.note: low confidence: only figure found is a third-party blog table (Introl, Jan 2026) listing 20-30 C supply; that blog also misstates CPU count and power. No AMD or OEM figure published; confirm with the OEM.

rack_pressure_drop_kpa.note: not published by AMD or OEMs as of 2026-10.

flow_lpm_per_kw.note: press report: rear manifolds draw roughly 385 L/min from the facility loop; divided by 245 kW and 225 kW.

thermal.quick_disconnect: Rear blind-mate quick disconnects (BlindMate QD) on the cooling manifold; QD size/type not published

width_mm.note: press report: ORW double-width frame spans 1200 mm (47.25 in); matches the EMCOR ORW frame datasheet (emcor-orw). Occupies two 600 mm slots.

depth_mm.note: press reports (ITdaily, StorageReview) give 1.3 m deep; the EMCOR ORW frame datasheet lists 1,219 mm. Range covers both; OEM depth may differ.

height_mm.note: press report: 94 in tall frame (Data Center Richness); matches the EMCOR ORW frame datasheet height of 2,390 mm.

rack_units.note: press report of AMD Hot Chips 2026 slide: 44 OU ORW-HPR chassis (OpenU = 48 mm), 18 compute + 6 switch trays.

weight_kg.note: reports conflict: DCD launch coverage (July 2026) says ~5,000 lb (2,267 kg); Lisa Su at CES (Jan 2026; sources techcrunch-helios-weight, dcr-helios) said nearly 7,000 lb (3,175 kg). Compute trays weigh ~77 kg each (itdaily-helios). Use the high end for floor loading until the OEM confirms.

feet.note: assumed four corner leveling feet; not published. A 1.2 m wide frame carrying up to ~3.2 t may use extra mid-span feet; confirm point loads with the OEM.

service_clearance_front_mm.note: not published; front access is needed to pull ~77 kg compute trays (lift assist likely).

service_clearance_rear_mm.note: not published; rear access is needed for the busbar, power shelves and coolant manifold.

scale_out_ports.note: AMD: up to 2.4 Tb/s scale-out per GPU using 800G Vulcano NICs, so 3 NICs x 72 GPUs = 216 ports. This matches AMD's 43 TB/s (216 x 800 Gb/s x 2 directions). The 2-NIC-per-GPU option gives 144. Excludes 18x Salina 400G front-end DPUs.

port_speed_gbps.note: AMD Pensando Vulcano 800 AI NIC, single 800G Ethernet port, UEC-ready

scale_up_domain.note: 72 GPUs over UALink over Ethernet (UALoE) through 6 switch trays, single hop

scale_up_bandwidth_tbps.note: AMD: 260 TB/s aggregate scale-up bandwidth (= 2,080 Tb/s), i.e. ~3.6 TB/s bidirectional per GPU

switch_slots.note: compute rack. Its 6 internal UALoE scale-up switch trays (~7 kW each, liquid-cooled) are part of the rack; there are no slots for scale-out leaf switches.

network.port_media: 800G Ethernet (Pensando Vulcano, one 800G port per NIC); inter-rack links are typically optics; scale-up is internal copper

cpus.note: one EPYC Venice (6th Gen, SP7) per 4-GPU compute tray, 18 trays

fp4_pflops.note: 2.9 EF peak OCP MXFP4 dense (~40 PF per GPU); AMD engineering projection
